# Go: this feed first, then the public proxy
# Warning: Do not list these modules in GOPRIVATE: it sets GONOPROXY too, so Go skips every proxy, this feed included, and goes to the module path's host directly.
# The feed answers only for its own modules (go.acme.dev,example.com/acme) and 404s every other path, so Go moves on to the public proxy for everything else. GONOSUMDB keeps these modules away from the public checksum database, which cannot see them; go.sum still pins every hash.
go env -w GOPROXY=https://pkg.plrs.im/go/acme,https://proxy.golang.org,direct
go env -w GONOSUMDB=go.acme.dev,example.com/acme

# Go: the feed credentials
# The go command sends a .netrc entry's login and password as HTTP Basic credentials to the proxy's host.
printf 'machine %s login __token__ password %s\n' pkg.plrs.im "$PKEY_REGISTRY_TOKEN" >> ~/.netrc

# Depend on the module
go get go.acme.dev/<module>@latest
